newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia crudes mark time, futures steady.
newsitem.headline: Asia crudes mark time, futures steady.

text.p: Asian crude prices on Tuesday marked time as both benchmark Brent and NYMEX crudes held steady.
The Brent October contract, trading on SIMEX, was traded near the close at $22.59 per barrel, down two cents from the London settlement of $22.61.
NYMEX crude, trading on the screen-based system ACCESS, was last traded at $23.76 per barrel, up three cents from the New York close.
Brokers said tension in Iraq would keep the market supported if it did not spark fresh buying interest.
A Baghdad-backed Kurdistan Democratic Party swept through Iraq to capture the main northern town of Sulaimaniya on MOnday from the oppositon Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).
The buoyant price of Brent was keeping the November Brent/Dubai near $2.00. It was quoted on Tuesday at $1.90/$2.00, little changed from $1.95/$1.98 a day earlier.
Dubai intermonth spreads for November/December and December/January were steady at 39/45 cents.
Paper Tapis was also steady, quoted at $21.65/$22.00 per barrel for October.
Traders said little wet trading was underway owing to traders' participation in an industry conference in Singapore.
Industry sources said there was just more than 1.3 million barrels of Tapis available for October. A producer said the firm market was pushing Tapis premiums to $1.00 per barrel.
However, on the basis of last done Labuan at 90 cents, Tapis would be valued around 80 cents.
One trader said an October Minas was said done at a discount to the ICP of 20 cents, but he questioned the deal because nominations were not yet settled.
